security_audit.summary: All 37 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documented Codex paths, and benign environment or path handling. The bundled scripts perform intended local plan operations without network access or dynamic command execution. One medium-severity symlink overwrite risk remains when --overwrite follows an existing plan-path link.

remediation.suggestion: Reject symbolic-link destinations before writing, then open the file with no-follow and exclusive safety checks to prevent redirected overwrites.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink-Following Plan Overwrite
semantic_findings.description: With --overwrite, write_text follows an existing symbolic link at the plan path. A crafted link could redirect the write to another user-writable file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The destination is checked for existence but never checked for symbolic links before write_text truncates it. Exploitation requires a preexisting crafted link and overwrite use.

content.value_statement: Implementation work becomes difficult when plans are scattered or inconsistent. This skill creates, finds, validates, updates, and stores structured Codex plan documents.
actual_capabilities: Draft implementation plans with requirements, scope, file targets, ordered actions, validation, risks, and open questions.
Create overview plans that document architecture, flows, behavior, status, and key file references.
Store Markdown plans with validated names and minimal frontmatter in the local Codex plans directory.
List stored plans and filter summaries by a case-insensitive query.
Read and validate the name and description from a specific plan.
Update, rename, or delete stored plans after confirming the requested change.
limitations: It does not implement tasks or modify repository code.
Stored plans require local filesystem access to CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex/plans.
The helper scripts require Python 3 and provide no graphical interface.
Frontmatter supports only single-line name and description values.

use_cases.title: Plan a feature implementation
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into ordered work, file targets, tests, risks, and open questions before coding begins.

use_cases.title: Document an existing system
use_cases.description: Capture architecture, data flow, authentication, routing, key files, and current behavior without creating an implementation checklist.

use_cases.title: Maintain shared plan records
use_cases.description: Find, validate, revise, rename, or remove stored plans as requirements and project context change.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [feature]. Include requirements, scope, files, action items, tests, risks, and open questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a feature needs a clear starting plan.

prompt_templates.title: Find and compare plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Find plans related to [topic]. Summarize each match, validate its frontmatter, and ask me to choose if several plans match.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when existing work may already be documented.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a stored plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the plan named [plan-name] for [changed requirement]. Recheck relevant repository files, preserve its name, and revise validation and risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this after requirements or implementation context changes.

prompt_templates.title: Map a complex system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an overview plan for [system]. Map architecture, data flow, authentication, routing, key files, current status, and unresolved risks. Add a Mermaid diagram when useful.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced architecture or operational reference documentation.

output_examples.input: Create an implementation plan for adding profile image uploads.
output: Goal: add validated profile image uploads with clear storage and size limits.
Scope: profile API, storage adapter, upload validation, cleanup behavior, and user-facing errors.
Validation: unit tests, integration tests, unsupported-format checks, oversized-file checks, and replacement cleanup.

output_examples.input: Find plans about rate limiting and summarize the best match.
output: Summary: documents current request limits, retry behavior, affected entry points, and pending decisions.
Status: frontmatter is valid and the plan name matches its filename.

output_examples.input: Create an overview plan for the authentication flow.
output: Overview: traces sign-in from the client through session validation and protected routing.
Key references: authentication middleware, session storage, route guards, and callback handlers.
Open risk: clarify token refresh behavior when a session expires during an active request.

best_practices: Inspect relevant repository documentation and entry points before drafting a plan.
Keep action items ordered, concrete, and linked to likely files or modules.
Confirm user intent before overwriting, renaming, or deleting a stored plan.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, credentials, or private tokens in plan bodies or descriptions.
Do not use invalid names, extra frontmatter keys, or multiline frontmatter values.
Do not treat an overview plan as approval to modify repository code.

faq.question: Does this skill modify repository code?
faq.answer: No. It reads repository context and writes only plan documents in the configured Codex plans directory.

faq.question: Where are plans stored?
faq.answer: Plans are stored under CODEX_HOME/plans, or ~/.codex/plans when CODEX_HOME is not set.

faq.question: Which plan styles are supported?
faq.answer: It supports ordered implementation plans and overview plans for architecture, flows, behavior, or reference material.

faq.question: Can it manage existing plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It can find, read, validate, update, rename, and delete existing plan documents.

faq.question: What format does a stored plan use?
faq.answer: Each plan is Markdown with name and description frontmatter followed by a free-form plan body.

faq.question: Does the skill use network services?
faq.answer: No. The included helpers use local filesystem operations and make no network requests.
